Chrome pegs, a gyro and a sticker-bombed frame. Every estate in Hackney has three. The Chainring pays £40–60 for a clean one.
Front suspension, knobbly tyres, a D-lock that is usually better than the bike. Goes over the Marshes, down the towpath and through Victoria Park.
A featherweight carbon racer worth more than most of the cars on Mare Street. Its owner locks it to a lamppost with two locks and a prayer.
Twenty kilos of red steel from a docking station. Anyone can ride one; nobody will buy one. Untraceable, so the cops do not care.
A rental scooter with the speed limiter ripped out. Silent, foldable, illegal on the road and everywhere else.
Pedal-assist bike with an insulated box on the back. Start a Courier shift from the driver seat to take delivery jobs.
The noise of every high street at 11pm. Top box, pillion seat, L-plates optional. Doubles as a courier bike.
An unregistered off-road bike that wheelies the length of the Marshes. No plate, no insurance, no brakes worth mentioning.
A naked 650 commuter bike. Light, quick, forgiving, parked outside every pub in Shoreditch.

Britain's favourite small car, therefore Britain's most stolen small car. A screwdriver and some nerve.

A dad's estate car with a roof box and a dog guard. Nobody looks twice at it, which is the whole point.
Keyless entry, tinted glass, never once off-road. A relay box and twenty seconds, if you know what you are doing.
A hand-built British grand tourer. Mayfair money parked on a Hoxton street.
A V12 wedge on a sheikh's plates. Seen in Knightsbridge, very occasionally in Shoreditch, never twice.
An imported American muscle car with a blower through the bonnet. Loud enough to set off car alarms in Dalston.
A dented white Transit-style van with "NO TOOLS LEFT IN THIS VEHICLE" on the back doors (there are tools). Courier jobs; also the classic getaway.
Plays "Greensleeves" at 90 decibels. Sells cones, and, everyone on the estate knows, rather more than cones.
Battenburg-livery response car: lights, siren, ANPR plate scanner, cage in the back. Start a Police shift from the driver seat.
The riot van. Six seats, four of them behind a cage.
Armed Response Vehicle. When one of these turns up you are on four stars.
Front-line ambulance: lights, siren, a stretcher bay. Start a Paramedic shift and get patients to Homerton or the Royal London.
A fire engine with a 13.5 m ladder and 1,800 litres of water. Start a Firefighter shift to answer fire calls.
A red double-decker on the 38 to Victoria (it never gets past Dalston). Start a Bus shift to run the route stop to stop.
Police air support. It flies over the street grid, sees everything and tells every car on the radio. Appears at three stars.

text.content:
THE SMOKE / 01 · Player Guide

The Smoke

You live in the gap between the rent and the next payday. Hackney is your patch. The Chainring is your crew. Auntie Pat has a workshop under the railway and a steady demand for bicycles nobody can provide a receipt for.

This is a crime sandbox about risky choices, loyal friends and the city pushing back. Take a small job, find a better angle, get paid, lose the Heat, and decide what kind of person you are becoming.

Before the first night

Agree the tone and boundaries together: comic capers, grounded crime, or something between them. Decide how the table wants to handle police violence, injury, addiction, debt and bystanders. Any player can pause the fiction. Nothing in the opening requires cruelty to uninvolved people.

Your first five clicks

Open your character. Click a stat to roll. Open the Blower with the phone icon or Alt+B. Right-click a vehicle to choose a seat. Move to a map exit and use its travel button.

THE SMOKE / 01 · Player Guide

The top strip

Health is how much punishment you can take. Hustle buys an edge before a roll. Cash is what you have on you. Heat stars tell you how hard the police are looking. Open your Blower for current work and instructions.

On the Street

Nine stat cards show your die and its modifier. Click the name to roll; the small selector changes the die when building or advancing a character. Guard is your passive attack target. Armour reduces damage. On a Roll and Off Your Game apply to your next roll and then clear.

Ready to hand lists weapons. Target someone with T, then click the weapon. Unarmed is always available. First aid rolls Savvy and posts a treatment button for the patient’s owner or the GM. Heal and Damage are direct bookkeeping tools for agreed effects.

Kit & Perks

Weapons, worn armour, gear and perks are listed separately. Use, edit or remove an item with its buttons. Drag an item from the equipment compendium to your sheet. Wear one armour item; equipping another removes the old one’s bonus.

Conditions

Every condition shows what it does and how to clear it. Active conditions are highlighted. Click one to add or remove it after recovery. Dice penalties and Guard changes apply automatically. Bleeding is handled during combat turns.

Identity

Your alias, ends, crew, ambition and bonds are editable. Use the story and notes editors to keep the people who matter close. Stashed cash is separate from cash in your pocket. Advances and Rep stage track growth.

THE SMOKE / 01 · Player Guide

Nine stats. A life outside the job.

Start with exactly one d8, three d6 and five d4. Everyone starts with Health 10, Hustle 3 and £40. The character builder checks the spread before applying it. Choose a name, day hustle, ambition and somebody you cannot casually abandon.

StatUse it for
MuscleForce, hand-to-hand fighting and grapples
GritEndurance, resisting pain and keeping conscious
MovesRunning, climbing, sneaking and dodging
WheelsDriving or riding
AimShooting and throwing
GraftLocks, repairs and deft hands
SavvyStreet knowledge, observation and first aid
FrontCharm, lies, negotiation and intimidation
BottleNerve and keeping your head

Pregens

Jaz Kaur is the rider and mechanic. Danny “Tealeaf” Doyle is the lock and the lie. Femi Adebayo reads the street and keeps people alive. Big Sal Moretti moves the heavy things and stands their ground. All four have a backstory, contacts, equipment and two situational perks.

THE SMOKE / 01 · Player Guide

Tell us what you want

Describe an intention and how you pursue it. The GM names a stat and a consequence for failure. Only roll when the outcome matters. The normal formula is Effort d6 + stat die + stat modifier. A die that rolls its maximum explodes: roll it again and add the result.

Died4d6d8d10d12d20
Modifier+2+3+4+5+6+10

Difficulty and help

Easy is about an 85% starting chance, Medium about 60%, Hard about 35%, and Long Shot about 12%. The exact target is solved from your unboosted dice; small variations occur because dice are discrete. The target stays fixed when you buy a perk or Hustle bonus.

Spend 1 Hustle to step your Effort die up. Spend 2 to become On a Roll for this roll. A relevant perk steps your stat die up once. Choose it in the dialog and explain why it fits. One perk applies; perks do not stack. A modifier is for an agreed situation, tool or advantage.

On a Roll makes each die explode on its highest two faces. Off Your Game suppresses explosions. If both apply, they cancel. In Pain suppresses the Effort die’s explosions even when the other die can still explode.

Read the result

Your total is compared with the target. The card shows the total, target, margin, outcome and explosions. One explosion is Nice One, two A Blinder, three Absolute Scenes, four or more Front Page. Those labels celebrate the roll; the GM fits the result to the fiction.

THE SMOKE / 01 · Player Guide

MarginOutcomeMeaning
−4 or worseProper MessFailure and a serious consequence
−3 to −1Bad LuckFailure; a limited success may be offered at a cost
0Just AboutSuccess with a complication
1–3SortedWhat you set out to do
4–7Smashed ItA strong result
8+LegendaryAn exceptional result

When the scene becomes a fight

Use the normal Foundry combat tracker. Initiative is d6 + your Moves modifier. On your turn take one action and move one zone; the GM may trade distance for a roll in a chase or difficult space. You have one reaction between your turns. Describe what the actions look like rather than looking for a list of combat powers.

Target a token, then use a weapon or Unarmed. Attacks roll against Guard. A hit produces a damage card: damage = margin + weapon Impact − armour, minimum zero. The target’s owner or GM chooses Take hit or Dodge. Dodge rolls Moves against the attacker’s total and spends the reaction even on failure. Each card can resolve once.

Armour only counts when equipped. Covered vehicle riders gain +2 Guard; exposed bicycle and motorcycle riders do not. A windowless load bay cannot attack out. Hand-to-hand attacks need adjacent tokens.

Conditions and getting help

The GM can choose one fitting damage condition; a severe injury is not an instruction to apply every listed condition. At 0 Health you are Down and cannot act. Grit can keep you conscious, but you still need help. A Proper Mess or three unassisted turns can lead to Wasted; the GM confirms the transition.

THE SMOKE / 01 · Player Guide

Get in

Stand beside a vehicle. Right-click it and choose Board / Choose seat. Pick the character and seat. The driver controls the vehicle; passengers remain separate PC/NPC tokens at half size, seated on the vehicle art. They move in the same update as the vehicle.

Locked vehicles must be unlocked in the fiction or nicked first. Moving traffic has a driver: use Carjack rather than Board. A successful theft unlocks the vehicle; it does not erase the consequences. Caged passengers need somebody else to open the cage.

Right-click your seated token to Get out or Change seat. Right-click the vehicle to inspect occupants, operate blue lights, scan a target plate, start a shift, or sell it at a suitable fence. The options depend on its kit and location.

Behind the wheel

The vehicle’s Performance die replaces Effort d6. Add its Handling. Blue lights give +1 Wheels. Ordinary vehicles take −2 off road; nimble vehicles avoid that penalty, and off-road vehicles get +1 there. Black cabs gain +1 at junctions. A wrecked vehicle’s Performance steps down once.

Traffic keeps left and follows the supplied road polylines. Its pauses, turning and police pursuit are a game abstraction. Movement remains under the GM’s judgement for collisions, difficult stunts and places a vehicle cannot fit.

Cross the city

The atlas has 20 connected street maps, a 5×4 overview and four interiors. Move to a marked road exit and right-click → Go to the next map. Everyone aboard travels together. Walk into a door to enter an interior. A vehicle approaching a building parks outside and sends the riders in when you select that door.

The travel picker can show destinations; the GM authorises long-distance travel. Players use local exits to make journeys. The Blower’s Directions button gives the map route for a job.

THE SMOKE / 01 · Player Guide

Someone saw

Only witnessed crimes add Heat. The GM’s witnessed-crime button records the event. Police seeing it add one further star. Keep a low profile if you want your work to stay small.

HeatResponse
0Clean
1A patrol has your description
2Area cars and bikes hunt
3India 99 helicopter overhead
4Trojan armed-response units
5Roadblocks on map exits

Get clear

Heat cools one star at a time while no police unit can see you: 45, 60, 90, 120 or 150 seconds at stars 1–5. Being inside removes the helicopter’s outdoor sight, but ground units and the fiction still matter. A marked stolen vehicle can attract ANPR attention.

At five stars, driving through an edge exit requires a Hard Wheels roadblock check. Failure stops the vehicle and deals 6 Body damage. Flying vehicles bypass roadblocks. This is the moment to consider a different plan.

Wasted and Busted

Wasted returns you to Homerton A&E with full Health and cleared Heat. Pocket loss is 10% with a £50 floor, capped by the cash you have. Broken persists for longer recovery. Busted sends you to custody, clears Heat and conditions, and confiscates weapons. The cash loss is 20% with a £100 floor, again capped by your cash. These are game penalties, not statements about real hospital charges or UK sentencing.

You do not lose cash already stashed at home. Agree what happened during the missing hours and who now remembers your face.

THE SMOKE / 01 · Player Guide

The Blower

Alt+B opens your phone. Choose an owned character, check cash and Heat, see current calls and accept or pass. Only the correct driver receives their shift. A call shows its instructions, timer, relevant roll button and Directions.

Take the driver seat in a taxi, police vehicle, ambulance, fire pump, courier vehicle or bus, then start a shift from its token or the phone. Ask Pat gives a bicycle order without a service vehicle. End a shift when you are finished. Call clocks use live time; the GM can pause them or slow them for a learning table.

A night’s kip

Lose your Heat and get to the flat or another safehouse. Rest restores Health and Hustle and removes everyday conditions. Broken, Bleeding, Cuffed and other significant states need their listed treatment or recovery. First aid stops Bleeding and restores 2 Health; it is not a way to repeatedly farm health during one quiet instant.

Move up

After a meaningful mission, the GM may award one advance. Spend it from Identity to step a stat up. Stage 1 caps permanent stats at d8, Stage 2 at d10, Stages 3–4 at d12, and Stage 5 allows d20. Rep stage rises at agreed campaign milestones. Temporary perk and Hustle upgrades follow their normal ladder rules.

Cash can buy better tools and breathing room, but people are the real campaign. Update your bonds, note who helped you, and decide what you owe them.

The GM guide contains the opening missions and secrets. You do not need another game system or any external module to play this package.

Use Local services on your sheet or the token’s right-click controls. Walk or drive to the marked service first; the dialog shows the price before you buy. Cash in your stash is protected. Prices can be changed by the GM in system settings.

Respray: drive to a respray shop out of police sight. The standard price is £100. It clears your Heat and changes the plate, removing the old ANPR marker; the car remains stolen for fencing. A helicopter watching you prevents the visit.

Change clothes: visit a clothes marker out of police sight. £25 removes one Heat star. Garage repair: respray shops, the chop shop and The Arches repair a vehicle for £10 per missing Body. Written-off vehicles need replacement or GM recovery.

First aid: target an injured person beside you, then click First aid. A successful Medium Savvy roll offers a one-use treatment card: the patient or GM applies it, restoring 2 Health and stopping Bleeding and Hurt. A new injury permits another treatment. Down patients return to at least 1 Health.

Rest: reach a safehouse with no Heat and stop Bleeding first. A night restores Health and Hustle and clears the listed short-term conditions. Broken remains until A&E and a week of recovery; the GM clears it when that time has passed.

Advance: the GM awards advances from Street Control. Spend one from Identity to step a stat up within your Rep cap: d8 at Rep 1, d10 at Rep 2, d12 at Rep 3–4, d20 at Rep 5. The GM can raise Rep at a milestone.

Target a foe and use a readied weapon. A hit posts its exact damage and offers the target Take hit or Dodge. Each attack resolves once; a successful Dodge prevents its damage and conditions. Only one listed condition can be chosen for a hit that lands.

Firearms spend one round per shot. Empty magazines cannot fire; use Reload to refill the magazine when the fiction permits. Three Bruises become Hurt. Bleeding costs 1 Health at the end of your turn. At 0 Health you are Down: you can only roll Grit to stay conscious until helped. After three rounds without aid, or a Proper Mess on that roll, the system sends you to A&E automatically. The GM can also resolve Wasted from the Down card.

THE SMOKE / 02 · GM Guide & The Chainring

Welcome to Hackney.

Begin with people and a small job. Teach the game through one lock, one conversation and one journey before escalating to a pursuit.

Set up

Launch a world using The Smoke, then open Street Control from the token tools or system settings. Set up the world imports the pregens, equipment, people, vehicles, guides and all London maps. It is safe to run again: existing documents are preserved. Assign each player a pregen in the setup dialog or through ownership afterwards.

The opening places the crew in Your Flat. Auntie Pat, Spanner Rob and Kez are at The Arches; Mo sends the crew round to meet them. Player-facing journals have Observer access; this GM book stays private. The guides compendium is hidden from normal player roles to keep its GM entries private.

Use a connected GM as the authority for vehicle movement and world actions. Job state is per driver and survives a browser refresh. A second GM can observe, but the active GM handles simulation. Start with police driving off and clocks paused until players understand the controls.

Running the sandbox

Ask what the crew needs money for today. Let useful local knowledge be true. When a roll matters, explain the risk before the dice. Turn a failure into a changed position, a witness, a bill, an awkward promise or a pursuit. Do not require violence to recover from an error.

THE SMOKE / 02 · GM Guide & The Chainring

Opening read-aloud

The train passes so close overhead that the tea trembles in its mug. Beneath the railway arch, a wheel turns in Spanner’s stand with a soft, steady tick. Auntie Pat is counting notes on a rubber mat. She looks up as you come in. “Right. Nobody’s dead, nobody’s late, and I’ve got a customer. Let’s try and keep all three of those things true.”

Introduce the crew

Ask each player where they slept, what is due before Friday, and who they last disappointed. Pat offers tea. Kez has two locations on their phone. Spanner lends bolt cutters if the party did not buy a set. Nobody starts owing a debt they did not agree to play.

Teach selecting a token and opening the sheet. Let each player make a harmless practice Medium roll. Explain that a practice result has no Heat. Open the Blower and show how to follow an instruction before turning the clocks on.

Campaign pressure clocks

Track Pat’s trust (0–4), the Lea Boys’ interest (0–4), and Vale’s case (0–4) in GM notes. A clean delivery raises trust. Public cruelty or lying about a loss lowers it. A visible incursion on Stretch’s patch raises interest. Repeated witnesses and plates raise the case. These are GM story clocks; they are distinct from the automated Heat stars.

THE SMOKE / 02 · GM Guide & The Chainring

The offer

“Two bikes, any sort worth a buyer’s time. I’ve got forty quid extra if you bring both. Kez knows a couple of places. Quiet work, alright?”

This is the training job: reconnaissance, one theft each, boarding, a journey, a fence and an unexpected human complication. Expected length: 60–90 minutes. Run clocks at ×2 or paused for the first attempt.

Prepare

Use Ask Pat for repeatable sandbox orders, or run this fixed opening manually. Put two locked ordinary bicycles on the pavements near named landmarks in Dalston or Haggerston; import a BMX and mountain bike from Motors. Set the locked flag through a token macro if needed, or use existing Street Life bicycles. Pat lends one pair of bolt cutters.

Kez’s first tip is outside a café off Dalston Lane: an Easy lock, people indoors, a delivery rider checking their phone. Second is near London Fields: a Medium lock, a cyclist searching their bag and a neighbour looking from a window. The bikes are not drawn into the map; they are vehicle tokens.

Play it

Savvy Medium identifies the observer before the crew approaches. Front Easy can start a conversation that draws attention away. A Graft theft roll uses the lock band, eased one band by bolt cutters or two by an angle grinder. Resolve the theft through Nick it so unlocking, stolen markers and Heat stay connected.

On a clean result, let the crew ride off. On Just About, somebody films the wrong bit of the scene. On Bad Luck the lock holds and the crew must change the plan. On Proper Mess, the alarm or witness forces an immediate choice; a patrol arrives if Heat warrants it. Do not roll for every metre of pavement.

The human turn

One bicycle carries a child’s rain cover and a note from a parent who uses it for work. The crew can replace that target, return it, pay compensation or continue. Honour the choice. Pat accepts a different bike and does not demand that this person be ruined.

Pay and fallout

Sell outside The Arches from the vehicle HUD. Each bike pays its fence value. Award the £40 fixed-job bonus manually, or use the automatic order’s advertised bonus if running Ask Pat. Each player earns one advance. A public scene adds Vale’s first witness; a thoughtful solution adds Pat’s trust. Seed Mission 2 with a white van that passed both locations.

THE SMOKE / 02 · GM Guide & The Chainring

The offer

Spanner slides a relay box across the bench, still in its foam. “That van took something of Pat’s. Not the van. What’s in it. Bring the box home. Ask questions if you have to. Preferably before anyone gets hit.”

Expected length: 90–150 minutes. The van is a means of moving the scene, not a puzzle about real vehicle security. Resolve its lock as a fictional Graft test.

Prepare

Place two Tranzit vans around Homerton East & Wick Woodland. One is a harmless tradesperson’s van. The other has a replaced door panel, a crate visible through its open rear door and a Lea Boy near it. Use tokens, parked cars and existing road locations. There is no new mandatory interior.

The crate holds a workshop diagnostic unit worth £350 and a payment book that ties Danny’s debt to Stretch. Pat wants the unit. Stretch wants the book. Vale wants somebody to admit either exists.

Find the right one

Savvy Medium spots the replaced panel; Front Medium gets a useful answer from a worker. Taking the first matching model without a look brings the wrong owner and a moral problem, but it does not dead-end the mission. If the crew follows a plate rather than a person, give them an actual lead, not a random false negative.

The Lea Boy’s name is Leon. He owes money and thinks the crate is ordinary stolen tools. Front Hard can convince him he is being used. A clean promise to help him later changes this to Medium. Muscle can seize the box; use a physical tracked challenge at 3 progress / 3 consequences if several people get involved.

The moving scene

If alerted, Stretch’s driver leaves in the van. The crew may follow in a vehicle or cut through the Woodland on bicycles. Start a chase at gap 2: Sorted closes 1, Smashed It closes 2, Legendary closes 3, Bad Luck opens 1, Proper Mess opens 2 and causes a collision. At gap 0 the van is boxed in; at gap 5 it gets clear. The GM can track this pursuit in notes while moving across the linked maps.

An alternative is a call to Vale. She will recover the unit as evidence and offer the crew a conversation rather than cash. Pat dislikes losing it but respects being told what happened.

Pay and fallout

Recovering the unit pays £200 to split, plus £60 for the crew’s time. A sensible attempt that leaves the unit with police still earns £60. Award one advance each. The book reveals Stretch’s next collection at Bow; keeping a copy gives the crew bargaining power in Mission 3.

THE SMOKE / 02 · GM Guide & The Chainring

The offer

Pat does not count the money this time. She puts the book on the counter and rests her hand on it. “He can have his debt. He doesn’t get to have my people.”

Expected length: 2–3 hours. This closes the first arc and opens the wider sandbox. Success means the crew chooses a future; it need not mean defeating every enemy.

Prepare

Stretch has arranged a collection on the road by Bow Breakers Yard, on the Old Ford & Bow map. He arrives with two Lea Boys, a parked white van and a bike intended as collateral. Give each NPC a visible reason to leave before a fight begins. The collection is for a frightened tenant connected to Mo.

Vale has a copy of one plate and a partial witness statement. She will attend a meeting if the crew offers specific evidence. Pat can contribute £100 but will not abandon the shop. Kez can warn the tenant and arrange an exit.

Three working plans

Negotiate: Front Hard, or Medium with the payment book and a credible alternative, against a 4-progress / 3-consequence social challenge. Savvy can expose a discrepancy; Bottle can hold a boundary; Muscle can move a blocking vehicle without injuring anyone. Each contribution needs a new fictional approach.

Expose: deliver the book and a willing witness to Vale. Use a 3-progress / 3-consequence challenge involving Front to build trust, Savvy to verify the pages and Wheels to keep the meeting safe. Vale protects the witness and opens a case; she does not erase the crew’s other crimes.

Steal the leverage: take the collateral and the ledger copy while keeping the tenant out of danger. Use the map’s routes, a distraction and a chase if it goes wrong. A vehicle must be unlocked, boarded and driven normally; people do not teleport because a plan sounded good.

If it turns violent

Stretch uses Muscle d8, Grit/Bottle/Moves d6 and a knife; two Lea Boys are ordinary local enforcers. Scale numbers down for fewer than four PCs. They retreat when their plan is gone or a friend is badly hurt. Witnesses add Heat, which can make fleeing wiser than winning. Firearms should feel like a new problem, not a routine reward.

End the arc

A freed tenant and a crew that stands together earn Pat’s trust, one advance each, and Rep Stage 2 at the table’s discretion. Cash reward: £300 shared, plus any legitimate job pay earned along the way. Stretch may lose the patch, cut a deal or promise revenge. Vale becomes a contact with boundaries. Ask every player what they spend their share on before offering the next job.

THE SMOKE / 02 · GM Guide & The Chainring

Police are a pressure system

Heat is fast, visible and local. Evidence, reputation and relationships are slower campaign consequences. Clearing stars does not delete a witness from the story. Use police response settings to match the table: manual unit movement is useful while learning, automatic pursuit makes a chase immediate.

A helicopter sees outdoors on its map; the automatic model does not calculate walls or detailed real-world surveillance. The GM should override an implausible sighting, paused patrol or inappropriate response. A roadblock check triggers once per edge crossing at five stars, before the convoy transfers.

Vehicles

Do not grant player ownership of every parked vehicle. Boarding gives the seated driver control of the specific vehicle. Convoy moves use one scene batch, and token IDs are remapped on transit. The original footprint is restored on exit. A failed setup request or disappearing passenger is a reason to run diagnostics before continuing the scene.

Resolve a risky stunt with Wheels, not a series of pixel-perfect drags. A standard collision deals 4 Body; an agreed high-speed or roadblock collision can deal 6. At zero Body a vehicle is wrecked and suffers one Performance step down; another damaging hit writes it off. Eject passengers before deleting a vehicle if the fiction calls for escape.

Money and growth

Emergency service rewards are arcade pay, not actual employment or UK public-service salaries. Wasted/Busted costs are game loss rules, not real fees. Cash prices are fictional balancing figures. Keep the table’s money scale consistent.

Award one advance after a completed mission or a comparably meaningful failure. Rep stage rises when the fiction supports a wider patch: Stage 2 after the opening arc, Stage 3 when the crew controls a reliable income, Stage 4 when the borough knows them, Stage 5 for legends. Choose those milestones together.

THE SMOKE / 02 · GM Guide & The Chainring

Clock controls

The default callout timer is live time. Job Clock ×2 doubles deadlines. Pause Job Clocks freezes calls, offers and patient deterioration together, including their countdown display. Resume shifts all relevant timestamps by the paused interval. Pausing Foundry also stops traffic and hunting.

A long session break should use Pause Job Clocks. End a shift before retiring its vehicle. A shifted vehicle is identified by its shift flag after a map transfer, so the driver’s work follows the convoy. Only the driver or GM can accept, decline or end that shift.

Street Control

Populate seeds moving cars, parked cars, locked bikes and pedestrians. Clear removes generated ambient life and protects occupied, stolen and active job tokens. Police respond adds the units the current Heat requires. Stand down removes generated response units without changing Heat; turn automatic response off as well if you need a quiet scene.

Put a shift on the map creates an unlocked issued vehicle beside a selected PC. This is a scenario tool: borrowing it from Street Control is not treated as stealing an emergency vehicle. A police car stolen from the hunt is a different story.

Recover without starting again

The setup operation only adds missing content. It does not replace edited characters or notes. Importing a missing map is automatic when the crew travels there. Scene background repair handles v14 Level images. Diagnostics checks map exits, packs and rider references.

If a player sees somebody else’s call, first confirm which character they own. Multiple players owning the same actor share control by design. Each shift still belongs to its driver actor. Job chat is whispered to those owners and GMs. The phone only lists calls for the selected owned actor.

THE SMOKE / 02 · GM Guide & The Chainring

Twelve things that could happen next

  • Kez’s phone is stolen, and the thief is using it to accept Pat’s orders.
  • A courier offers a sealed envelope as payment for a repair.
  • A customer wants the bicycle they bought from Pat returned to its previous owner.
  • Spanner’s diagnostic unit shows that several vehicles share an impossible service history.
  • Vale needs a quiet driver for an off-the-record witness meeting.
  • Mo’s landlord arrives with a new padlock and a timetable.
  • A hire bike keeps reappearing outside the flat, no matter where the crew leaves it.
  • Leon wants out of the Lea Boys and has nowhere safe to go.
  • The cab driver recognises a passenger from a photograph Danny keeps folded in his wallet.
  • A fire callout happens at the building where the crew stashed their cash.
  • The person buying cars at Bow Breakers starts paying in favours.
  • A legal courier contract pays less than theft but could give the crew a real exit.

End on a choice

Offer a phone call, a person at the door or a name the crew recognises. Give the next session something specific to begin with. The city should grow out of their choices rather than resetting between jobs.

The active GM upgrades an existing v0.1.0/v0.1.1 world once on login. Missing content is added; existing actor stats, cash, items, notes and player assignments are preserved. Recorded driver grants are removed from shared vehicle templates and reapplied to dedicated vehicles.

The overview is above four north–south street folders, ordered west–east. Import every London map fills gaps without moving scenes you filed in your own folders. Setup opens the flat for a new world, puts the pregens there and provides starter job vehicles on Hackney Central.

All equipment from both branches is included. GM books and missions are private; the Player Guide, work handbook, rules reference, directory and kit guide are visible as world journals. A GM must remain connected for rolls, shared resources, services and jobs.

Local services use configurable prices. Broken injuries still require the stated week of fictional recovery after A&E. Heal/remove conditions from the sheet when that recovery is complete. Use the combat tracker for automatic Bleeding, reaction resets and Down countdowns.

Pause clocks before leaving the game. Offer expiry, patient deterioration and every deadline pause together and survive a reload. The automated checks use a Foundry contract harness; follow VALIDATION.md for the licensed Foundry/Forge acceptance run.

THE SMOKE / 03 · Work the Borough

A vehicle, a driver, a call

The GM can issue a service vehicle from Street Control. Board it as driver and Start shift. Your phone shows the shift and dispatch offers. Accept starts the job; Pass gives dispatch another chance later. Only one shift per driver and one active call per shift.

The countdown is live time. For a turn-based or learning table, the GM can pause job clocks or use a slower clock multiplier. A shift’s pay goes to its driver. Agree how the crew splits that money. End shift posts the earned total and clears that shift’s calls.

Callouts are arcade fiction. These procedures are game instructions and do not teach real emergency response, policing or vehicle access.

THE SMOKE / 03 · Work the Borough

Taxi

Accept the fare, follow Directions and pull up beside the hailing person. The game boards the fare in a free passenger seat. Drive to the named destination and stop on the adjacent road. Reaching it pays the fare and tip.

Some fares are in a hurry: the timer is shorter and the tip doubles. Make conversation with Front for a better tip; you get one conversation result per fare. Damage to your cab still matters to the story even when a passenger says it is “fine”.

Courier

Collect the order at its named zone, then reach the destination on the correct map. Pickup and delivery use separate clocks. A quick, undamaged run pays best; damage to the vehicle after collection reduces the pay. You do not need a passenger seat.

THE SMOKE / 03 · Work the Borough

Find the actual car

Accept the sweep. Dispatch gives a model, not the answer. The stolen car is seeded among decoys, including a clean car of the same model. Target a vehicle with T, then use ANPR from your police vehicle’s HUD. You must be within 12 squares.

The plate result includes keeper information and any reported-stolen marker. The correct scan advances the call. Blue lights on, get within five squares, and signal the driver to stop with Front. A clean same-model decoy is a useful reminder: scan plates rather than choosing by appearance.

Stop, pursue, arrest

A successful stop makes the target pull over. Get out and stand beside it, then use the arrest button. A failed stop starts a pursuit at gap 2. Wheels closes the gap; failure opens it. At zero the car is boxed in; at five it escapes.

Cuffing uses Muscle. On success the suspect is placed in a free caged passenger seat and the phone names the nearest police station. If there is no cage or no free seat, make room or obtain a suitable vehicle before the arrest can complete. Drive to the station’s adjacent road to book them in.

THE SMOKE / 03 · Work the Borough

A pursuit already in progress

Some calls begin with a fleeing vehicle. Follow the Wheels roll on the callout or your phone. A Proper Mess is a collision and 4 Body damage. A clean arrest pays more than a messy one. The chase continues on its gap track while the GM adjudicates the map movement.

A disturbance

Drive to the reported location. Front can calm the situation; Muscle can arrest the ringleader. A failed attempt to calm the group raises the stakes rather than automatically ending the call. A successful arrest still needs a custody drop-off.

Having a police shift does not grant the player the right to damage or arrest other PCs without agreement. The game mechanics support a duty scenario; the table sets its social boundaries.

THE SMOKE / 03 · Work the Borough

Treat, load, deliver

Accept the call and reach the patient. The phone changes to Treat & load. Roll Savvy; the result moves the patient along the condition ladder. A passenger seat with stretcher kit is preferred. An ambulance with no free patient seat must make room before loading.

Stable → Fading → Faltering → Passing → Lost. Untreated non-Stable patients worsen every 45 seconds of normal clock time. A strong treatment improves them two steps, Sorted one step, Just About holds, Bad Luck worsens one, Proper Mess two. Lost is final for that callout.

Loading changes the destination to the nearest hospital. Blue lights improve Wheels and stop traffic nearby. You can treat in the back during the journey through the phone. Reaching A&E pays according to the patient’s state.

THE SMOKE / 03 · Work the Borough

Firefighter

Drive to the fire marker. The call changes to Fight. Roll Grit to put progress on the fire: Sorted +1, Smashed It +2, Legendary +3, Just About +1 progress and +1 consequence, Bad Luck +1 consequence, Proper Mess +2 consequences. Put it out at 4 progress before 3 consequences lose the building.

If both thresholds are crossed in the same roll, consequences take precedence: the building is lost. Evacuation remains a fictional priority even when the scoring track is about the structure.

Bus

Accept a route with several stops, often crossing to a neighbouring map. Stop on each indicated road zone in order. Each stop pays for punctuality; finishing the route adds a bonus. This is a fictional local route rather than a claim that the real route 38 makes these exact stops.

THE SMOKE / 03 · Work the Borough

Ask Pat

Open the Blower and Ask Pat. The order belongs to that character. Kez supplies tip-offs on nearby maps. The requested bikes are seeded when those maps are visited; vehicles elsewhere that match the order also count.

Nick the bike, board as driver, ride it to The Arches and sell it from the vehicle HUD. Pat pays the fence value, and the order tracks matching deliveries. The final required delivery pays its advertised bonus. Sell one physical vehicle once; it disappears from the map after everyone gets out.

The default order clock is 30 minutes. Read the requested type: an order for a carbon road bike will not complete when you bring a BMX. Docking-station bikes are not accepted by a fence. Emergency-service vehicles are also unsellable.

pages.name: Two crews, map crossings and paused shifts

text.content:
The Blower lists your own calls and eligible ambulance/fire crew assistance. Only the driver can accept, pass or end their shift. A GM can manage any shift. Job rolls keep their prescribed stat and difficulty while still offering Hustle and relevant perks.

A taxi fare, patient or prisoner travels with the vehicle across map edges. The job keeps its new token references, and completion cleans up those passengers. Clear Street Life protects active targets and tipped-off bikes.

A full ambulance cannot proceed until the patient is in a stretcher bay. An arrest needs a free cage. Fires are lost if the consequences track fills, even when progress fills on the same roll.

THE SMOKE / 04 · Rules at a Glance

Dice and difficulty

Effort d6 + stat die + stat modifier. Both dice normally explode on their top face. Modifiers: d4 +2, d6 +3, d8 +4, d10 +5, d12 +6, d20 +10.

The GM chooses a band, which is solved from unboosted dice: Easy 85%, Medium 60%, Hard 35%, Long Shot 12%. An explicit target overrides the band. Temporary advantages improve the roll against that fixed target.

Hustle 1 steps Effort up. Hustle 2 buys On a Roll. One relevant perk steps the stat up. Temporary steps above d12 turn into +2 each before Stage 5. Off Your Game removes explosions; On a Roll explodes on the top two faces.

For teamwork, everyone rolls against the agreed target. Average totals, rounding down, then read the margin once. In a progress challenge, each meaningful contribution applies separately instead.

OutcomeProgressConsequences
Proper Mess02
Bad Luck01
Bad Luck, cost accepted11
Just About11
Sorted10
Smashed It20
Legendary30

THE SMOKE / 04 · Rules at a Glance

Turn structure

Initiative d6 + Moves modifier. One action and one-zone move per turn. One reaction refreshes at the start of your turn. Dodge is a Moves roll against the incoming attack total; a success avoids all of that hit, and a failed Dodge still spends the reaction.

Guard = 3 + base 4 + better of Moves/Grit modifier + equipped armour’s Guard bonus + condition changes. Covered riders gain +2. Vehicles use Guard 6 + twice Size.

An attack that reaches Guard hits. Damage = margin + Impact − armour reduction, minimum zero. One target owner or the GM resolves the hit card; it cannot apply damage twice. The GM may add one appropriate condition from the suggested severity.

DamageSeverityExamples
0NoneNo harm
1–2MinorBruised, Shaken, Prone
3–4ModerateHurt, Stunned, Restrained
5–6SevereBleeding, In Pain, Broken, Bricking It
7+CriticalDown, Broken, Bleeding

At zero Health the actor is Down. Bleeding costs 1 Health at the start of the actor’s turn. After three turns without aid, or a Proper Mess on Stay Conscious, the GM resolves Wasted. Stunned and Prone end when their stated recovery occurs; remove them in Conditions.

THE SMOKE / 04 · Rules at a Glance

Wheels

Vehicle Performance replaces Effort; Handling adds to the total. Blue lights +1. Normal off-road −2. Off-road kit +1 off road instead. Nimble kit avoids the penalty. Tight turning circle +1 at a junction. Wrecked Performance steps down once.

A standard chase starts at gap 2. Success closes the gap by its challenge progress, with Just About closing one. Bad Luck opens one; Proper Mess opens two and causes a collision. Catch at 0; lose at 5. A pursuit target is 4 + half the sum of the getaway driver’s Wheels and vehicle Performance faces, plus Handling, rounded.

Seats are exact: one driver, any extra crew positions, then passengers. Cages can only be opened from outside or a permitted front seat. Foldable vehicles must be empty before they can be carried.

Map scale

The map grid is a placement aid, not a fixed real-world distance. Zones represent meaningful stretches of road, junctions, blocks or rooms. Faint zone boundaries support range, destination and service checks; the traced road art is the driving path.

THE SMOKE / 04 · Rules at a Glance

CrimeHeat
Nick a bicycle or car1
Carjack2
Assault1
Assault a police officer2
Firing a gun2
Killing someone3
Killing an officer4
Failing to stop1
Dangerous driving1
Steal police vehicle3

Unseen crimes add no stars. A police witness adds one further star. Cap at five. Cool one star while out of sight for 45/60/90/120/150 seconds at Heat 1/2/3/4/5.

Wasted: lose max(£50, 10% pocket cash), capped at available cash. Busted: lose max(£100, 20%), capped likewise; weapons are confiscated. Both clear Heat. Stash is unaffected.

Fence value = original value × share × (0.4 + 0.6 × remaining Body fraction), reduced another 20% while hot, then rounded to £5. Pat’s bicycle share is 35%; the chop-shop motor share is 25%.

THE SMOKE / 04 · Rules at a Glance

Advances

The GM awards advances; one spends for a permanent stat step. Permanent caps by Rep stage: 1 d8; 2 d10; 3–4 d12; 5 d20. Rep stage is a campaign milestone, separate from crew/street/police relationship counters.

Safehouse rest with no Heat restores Health and Hustle and clears everyday fatigue and stress. First aid restores 2 Health and removes Bleeding/Hurt after a successful Medium Savvy roll. The GM limits repeated treatment by supplies and changing circumstances. A&E handles Wasted; Broken persists until the longer recovery is agreed.

Automation and judgement

The system automates dice, resources, hit resolution, listed condition penalties, convoy movement, Heat responses, ambient life, linked-map transit and shift callouts. It does not decide every social promise, legal consequence, collision or fictional prerequisite. Use the same clear standard for PCs and NPCs.

THE SMOKE / 05 · North & East London

One city. Twenty maps.

The atlas follows the supplied traced road geometry. It covers a playable slice of North and East London from Highbury to Stratford and Lea Bridge to Bethnal Green / Bow. Roads have been widened for tokens and labels: this is a game map, not a navigation service.

Each neighbouring map is linked at marked exits. The overview uses the same 5×4 arrangement as the street maps. Right-click at a district or exit to travel. The GM can import destinations on demand; a vehicle takes its occupants with it.

RowWest → East
NorthHighbury · Stoke Newington · Clapton · Hackney Marshes · Leyton
SecondCanonbury · Dalston · Hackney Central / Homerton · Homerton East / Wick Woodland · Olympic Park North
ThirdDe Beauvoir · Haggerston / London Fields · South Hackney / Well Street · Victoria Park / Hackney Wick · Stratford
SouthHoxton West / Canal · Haggerston Park / Hackney Road · Bethnal Green · Old Ford / Bow · Bow Flyover / Mill Meads

THE SMOKE / 05 · North & East London

The Arches · Pat’s Cycles

Morning Lane, on the Hackney Central map. A legitimate repair counter in front, working stands in the next arch, a loading yard and Pat’s office behind. Deliver stolen bikes to the adjacent road and use Sell to Auntie Pat. Walk through the marked door to speak with the crew.

Your flat above Chicken Palace

On the Hackney Central map. The shop downstairs belongs to Mo. The flat offers a safe place to sleep, talk and record what you owe. The safehouse rest action needs a token in or beside a safehouse zone and no Heat.

Mo has made the same request every time: keep trouble away from the shop. He means it.

THE SMOKE / 05 · North & East London

Homerton A&E

On the Hackney Central map. The ambulance callout drops patients at the hospital’s road zone; Wasted characters wake inside A&E. A curtain, a trolley and a nurse who knows when somebody is withholding the useful half of the story.

Custody suite

Linked to Stoke Newington police station. Busted characters arrive in the release area. This is an interior for aftermath, conversations and consequences rather than a procedural simulation of real detention.

Other services

Fire stations support scenarios. Taxi ranks and named landmarks offer callout destinations. Markets provide contacts and a place to change your look. Use Local services at a respray, clothes or repair marker. The dialog checks your location and quotes the configured price. Fencing uses Sell from the vehicle controls at the appropriate buyer.

THE SMOKE / 05 · North & East London

Dalston and Stoke Newington

Busy high streets, quieter side roads, markets and more observers than the crew first notices. Useful for a small theft with a large audience.

Haggerston, London Fields and the canal

Bicycles can choose routes a bulky van cannot. A pedestrian shortcut is useful until the person behind you knows it too. Keep the game’s path restrictions visible before a roll commits the plan.

Homerton, the Marshes and Wick

The Lea divides more than the map. Industrial yards, broad crossings and green space make pursuits feel different from the high street. Stretch’s influence lives in who answers the phone, not a painted border.

Stratford, Bethnal Green and Bow

Wider roads, busier destinations, the stadium and the breakers yard. A reliable place to earn money becomes somebody else’s reason to take notice.

THE SMOKE / 06 · The Chainring · Faces

Four people. One bad idea.

Jaz, Danny, Femi and Sal already know enough about each other to get in the same van. They do not have to agree about what happens when it stops. Read the full backstory on each character’s Identity tab; all four include their contacts and crew bonds.

Jaz Kaur

Wheels d8; Moves, Graft and Bottle d6. A courier with a mechanic’s hands and a garage-shaped ambition. Spanner’s good opinion matters to her. Bike Messenger and Grease Monkey are her situational edges.

Danny “Tealeaf” Doyle

Graft d8; Moves, Savvy and Front d6. A lock, a grin and a debt he does not quite explain. Pat gave him work when work mattered most. Locksmith and Silver Tongue fit the way he gets through a door.

Femi Adebayo

Savvy d8; Front, Bottle and Grit d6. He knows how to read a room and patch somebody up. His lines are clear even when keeping them is expensive. First Responder and Street Reader are his edges.

Big Sal Moretti

Muscle d8; Grit, Bottle and Wheels d6. Door staff, van driver and the person who says “leave it” before something becomes a fight. Door Staff and Hard to Shift are their edges.

THE SMOKE / 06 · The Chainring · Faces

Auntie Pat

The counter, the kettle, the ledger. Pat buys bikes, sets orders and values a quiet delivery. She protects the people who turn up for her, but she does not forget what something cost.

Spanner Rob

Mechanic and reluctant conscience. Ask him what is broken and he will tell you. Ask him why and you may get an answer you did not want.

Kez

Information has feet and a cracked phone screen. Kez knows where somebody parked and when they normally leave. They have plans of their own.

Mo Rahman

Chicken Palace’s owner and the flat’s anchor to an ordinary street. Kindness does not mean unlimited permission. He needs the business to survive whatever the crew brings home.

THE SMOKE / 06 · The Chainring · Faces

Stretch and the Lea Boys

Stretch calls coercion opportunity. The Lea Boys around him are people with loyalties, debts and varying enthusiasm for his plans. An encounter can end with a deal, a refusal or someone deciding to leave.

DS Harriet Vale

She follows the same people and the same plates until a pattern makes a case. A conversation with her can be a threat or a route out. She has limits; do not mistake patience for forgetting.

Add somebody

Each player should name one person outside the crew who would notice if they did not come home. Tell the GM what that person knows, what they need, and the one favour the character would struggle to refuse.

THE SMOKE / 07 · Tools, Money & Connections

Tools are an approach

Bolt cutters make a fictional bicycle lock one band easier. An angle grinder makes it two easier but is loud. A slim jim eases an ordinary motor lock one band; the fictional relay box eases compatible motor locks two. A screwdriver gives no automatic step. The theft roll abstracts the whole attempt.

The system chooses the best suitable tool the actor carries. A quantity of zero does not count. A jammed lock needs a changed plan or the GM’s intervention, rather than unlimited rerolls of the same attempt.

Other gear supplies fictional permission or a listed roll bonus. First-aid and vehicle-repair kits require a reasonable opportunity, supplies and time. An item’s price is a game figure; its availability comes from the scene.

pages.name: Weapons, protection and a way out

text.content:
THE SMOKE / 07 · Tools, Money & Connections

Keep the scale in mind

A bat or crowbar is already a serious choice. A firearm is rare, costly and conspicuous. Witnessed firing adds two Heat before any injury escalates the situation. A small crew can often win more through a useful witness or a working exit than a more powerful weapon.

One equipped armour item contributes Guard and damage reduction. Equipping another switches the worn item rather than stacking several jackets. A cycle helmet has fictional value without being an extra stacking armour bonus.

Perks

A perk is training in a specific situation. It steps the relevant stat up once when selected in the roll dialog. It is not a permanent bonus to every use of that stat. Explain why it fits before rolling.

THE SMOKE / 07 · Tools, Money & Connections

Sell the physical vehicle

Ride a stolen bicycle to The Arches or a stolen motor to Bow Breakers Yard. The HUD only offers the matching fence when you are beside its block. Fence pay depends on value, remaining Body and whether it is still hot. Everybody gets out before the sold token disappears.

Docking bikes and emergency vehicles are not accepted by the fence. A clean vehicle that belongs to you is not stolen stock, even if it has the same model as a nicked one.

Callout pay, fences and order bonuses credit the correct actor’s cash. The GM can handle a crew split through agreed sheet changes. Keep a simple record so buying food, tools or a night of peace still feels like a decision.

THE SMOKE / Hackney Missions — On Your Bike

ON YOUR BIKE

Start: Your Flat. Mo bangs on the door: rent is due Friday, and Pat "wants a word".

  1. Walk out through Chicken Palace onto Mare Street and round to The Arches on Morning Lane.
  2. Pat: "Two bikes by tonight. Nothing fancy. Kez'll show you where." (Phone → Ask Pat for work, or the GM hands out the order.)
  3. Kez rides with them to a bike rack — Street Life has chained bikes on every map; the tip-offs are on nearby maps.
  4. Nick two bikes (Graft). Teach the Heat rules the first time someone watches.
  5. Ride them back to The Arches and Sell to Auntie Pat.

Twist: one of the bikes belongs to a Lea Boy. He saw. Next session he wants it back — or Stretch does.

Pay: £40–60 a BMX, more for a mountain bike; order bonus £40.

THE SMOKE / Hackney Missions — On Your Bike

THE WHIPPET

Pat has a buyer for a Carbon Whippet road bike (worth £1,800 new). The Lycra lot chain them up outside the coffee places on Broadway Market (Haggerston & London Fields) and along the canal.

  • The lock is Hard. Bolt cutters make it Medium; the angle grinder makes it Easy — but loud. Broadway Market on a Saturday is full of phones.
  • If the owner comes back mid-job: Front to bluff ("I'm with the council, mate"), or Moves to leg it down the towpath.
  • Getaway: the Regent's Canal towpath runs west to Haggerston — bikes only, no police cars.

Complication: DS Vale has put a tracker in a bait bike on the same rack (the GM can mark one bike: Savvy, Hard to spot it). Nick the bait and a unit turns up at The Arches next session.

THE SMOKE / Hackney Missions — On Your Bike

LIGHTS AND SIRENS

The Lea Boys take Pat's van of stripped frames from outside The Arches. Pat wants it back before it crosses the Lea.

  • Steal something fast (or "borrow" the police car parked on Mare Street — +3 Heat if a copper sees).
  • Chase the van east along Morning Lane → Wick Road toward Hackney Wick: use the pursuit rules (Wheels each round, gap 2; 0 = boxed in, 5 = gone).
  • Or the clever route: run ANPR from the stolen area car on every van you pass. The GM can make the scanner flag Pat's van by setting a marker flag on its token (see the GM Guide).

Ending: catch the van on the Hertford Union bridge, face Stretch. Pay off, fight, or grass him to DS Vale (Pat will not like that).
